title: Shell completion end-to-end call path
answers: How does click shell completion work end to end?
Where is a completion request detected at runtime?
How are completion candidates produced for commands, options and params?
body:
Detection: core.py:Command.main → self._main_shell_completion(extra, prog_name, complete_var) runs BEFORE make_context/invoke; default complete_var is `_{PROG_NAME}_COMPLETE` (upper, `-`/`.`→`_`). Value format `{shell}_{instruction}` e.g. `bash_source`, `bash_complete`.
Dispatch: shell_completion.py:shell_complete(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var, instruction) picks a ShellComplete subclass (comp_cls) and runs `source` (prints script) or `complete` (prints candidates).
Script templates in shell_completion.py use %(complete_var)s/%(prog_name)s (bash/zsh/fish); user installs by eval'ing the program's `source` output (click never writes to disk).
Candidate resolution: shell_completion.py:_resolve_context / _resolve_incomplete (ends returning `ctx.command` or a param plus incomplete) → then obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete):
- core.py:Command.shell_complete: option names if incomplete starts with non-alnum; skips hidden and already-given non-multiple options; also chained-group sibling commands.
- core.py:Group.shell_complete: subcommands via _complete_visible_commands + super().
- core.py:Parameter.shell_complete: uses custom `shell_complete` callback (str results wrapped in CompletionItem) else type.shell_complete.
- types.py:ParamType.shell_complete default; overridden in Choice/File/Path etc.
